name: Hypericaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use opposite exstipulate gland-dotted leaves plus yellow 5-petal flowers with numerous stamens in bundles as the local Hypericum door.

project_scope.note: Both project taxa are accepted Hypericum, so the family lesson can be highly visual and genus-focused.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Hold a leaf to light: local Hypericum commonly shows translucent punctate glands and sometimes black marginal dots. Then confirm opposite simple exstipulate leaves and a yellow 5-petal flower packed with many stamens, often in distinct bundles.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs to shrubs. Local Hypericum has opposite simple leaves without stipules; translucent or dark gland dots/canals are highly useful.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually radial with 5 sepals and 5 free petals. Stamens are numerous and commonly united at the base into several bundles around a superior ovary.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a capsule in local Hypericum; styles/stigmas commonly 3–5 depending on the species group.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite leaves + no stipules + translucent/dark glands + yellow flower with many bundled stamens is a very strong local combination.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: leaf glands → opposite exstipulate node → yellow 5-petal flower → stamen bundles → capsule/styles → species doors
visual_lesson.intro: St. John's-worts become much easier when you use the leaf like a transparency slide. The glands are there even before the flower opens.

steps.title: 1 · Hold the leaf to light
steps.look_for: Translucent dots or short glandular canals; some taxa also show dark/black marginal or internal glands.
steps.why_it_matters: One of the fastest and most memorable Hypericum clues.

steps.title: 2 · Check the opposite node
steps.why_it_matters: Pairs the gland clue with a structural character and separates several lookalikes.

steps.title: 3 · Count petals, then ignore the exact stamen count
steps.look_for: Usually five yellow petals surrounding a dense mass of many stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: Many stamens are more useful than trying to count an exact number.

steps.title: 4 · See the stamens in bundles
steps.look_for: Filaments united at their bases into distinct groups around the ovary.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a strong family/genus-level reproductive clue.

steps.title: 5 · Finish with styles and capsule
steps.look_for: Superior ovary with multiple styles/stigmas, later becoming a dry capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirms the family after petals and stamens are gone.

comparisons.title: Hypericaceae vs Linaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be 5-petaled Malpighiales herbs, but Hypericum has opposite gland-dotted leaves and many stamens; local Linum usually has narrow leaves, only five fertile stamens and a five-style capsule plan.

comparisons.title: Hypericaceae vs Malpighiaceae
comparisons.rule: Both may show glandular structures, but Malpighiaceae often has clawed petals, 10 stamens and external sepal oil glands; Hypericum has numerous bundled stamens and translucent/dark leaf glands.

visual_lesson.caveat: Global Hypericaceae includes forms that depart from the familiar yellow Hypericum pattern. This project contains Hypericum only.

genera.fast_cue: opposite gland-dotted exstipulate leaves + yellow 5-petal flower + many bundled stamens

taxonomy_notes: Hypericum hypericoides and Hypericum walteri are both accepted under current Kew.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: circle pellucid glands and any dark glands
many bundled stamens vs five-stamen flax
